neighbours.label: the word-internal piece 'ib' or 'id' that closes a name or stem (Naj·ib, Hab·ib, Yaz·id, Rash·id, Cyan·id·ation); not names without the piece, and not 'id'/'ib' inside a one-token word (did, kid, rib)
fire: My neighbour Habib sells carpets in the old market.
The poet Ghalib wrote in both Urdu and Persian.
The striker Rashid scored twice in the second half.
Our guide Hamid met us at the gate of the old city.
The architect Zahid designed the new library.
A young clerk named Mujib kept the ledgers.
Her uncle Khalid owns a bakery near the harbour.
The singer Shakib performed at the festival.
quiet: My neighbour Hassan sells carpets in the old market.
The poet Hafez wrote in both Persian and Arabic.
The striker Omar scored twice in the second half.
Our guide Yusuf met us at the gate of the old city.
The architect did not hide the rib vaults of the new library.
A young kid named Robert kept the ledgers.
Her uncle Karim owns a bakery near the harbour.
The singer Leila performed at the festival.

notes: Card: 'ib' x3, 'id' x2, 'idine' x2 among the top 32 peaks, alongside ' cleaning', ' turtles' and ' dock', so the piece is one sub-trigger of several and coverage will be low.
